images.headline: The man who timed his own forgetting
images.prompt: Photojournalistic composite, 3:4 vertical, shot from a slightly low angle across a wooden desk. An elderly man in a plain 19th-century shirt and waistcoat sits at the desk, filling the upper two thirds of the frame, leaning forward with eyes closed and lips slightly parted mid-recitation, one hand pressed to his temple in effortful concentration, the other resting flat on a handwritten list of nonsense syllables — actively trying to hold the list in memory, not merely looking at it. An antique stopwatch lies open beside the list, its hands mid-tick. Utterly focused, alone, faintly obsessive. A single warm amber desk lamp is the only lit object, throwing a small pool of light across the desk while the room around him falls into cold shadow. Tiny illegible technical annotation text in the top-left corner, like a lab dossier, thin tick marks along the right edge. High contrast, deep blacks, fine film grain, documentary and unpolished, imperfect surfaces, dust in the light. images.headline: One look resets the curve
images.prompt: Ultra-detailed cinematic photograph, 3:4 vertical, shallow depth of field. A single candle wick with a nearly extinguished ember at its tip sits centred in absolute black void, filling the upper two thirds of the frame, a thin curl of smoke rising from it, the flame reduced to a faint orange glow about to die out. In the upper right, a circular inset cut-out shows an extreme macro close-up of the glowing wick tip, rendered sharper and brighter than the main scene. One warm amber practical light source: the ember glow itself, the only light in the frame, casting a small warm pool on the surface just below it.
